_comment: Hand-labelled ground truth for bench/frames_night (400 frames, 2026-08-29
18:15 through 2026-08-30 00:55, CSUSM Coffee Cart, 60s apart). This set
exists to answer one question the roadmap had open for months: does
StaticObjectFilter still have a job?
The plaza is lit at night. Mean frame brightness is 72.9 against a
MIN_FRAME_BRIGHTNESS gate of 15, so not one frame in this set would be
skipped as too dark in production. Whatever the detectors do here, they do
with a usable image.
Labelling method. Eyeballing 400 near-identical night frames is unreliable
in a way that biases the result, so candidates were found three ways and
the union was inspected:
1. bench/find_motion.py -- a temporal-median background and blob
detection, using pixels only, so the candidate list owes nothing to
either detector and can be used to score both. Run per lighting
segment: over the whole capture the dusk-to-night illumination change
swamps everything else.
2. Contact sheets over the sunset transition (frames 40-115), where the
background model is blind because the light is changing faster than
anything in the scene.
3. Every detection from both backends, cropped and magnified.
Frames not listed contain zero people. 396 of 400 are empty.

_notes.frame_150.jpg: Motion detector flagged a ~460px blob here and at 154. Both are the door-light glow shifting, not a person. Inspected at full resolution across 149-155.
_notes.frame_207.jpg: Two people walking across the lit plaza at roughly 21:40, clearly visible. YOLOv8n reported zero; LocateAnything-3B found both. The only night frame that separates the two backends.
